A1.statement: If labels are positive integers, independent composition multiplies labels, and a monotone size satisfies I(mn)=I(m)+I(n), then I(n)=c log(n), c>=0.
A1.regularity_caveat: Without monotonicity or an equivalent regularity condition, arbitrary values on primes extend to additive functions.
A1.proof: Compare n^floor(k log(m)/log(n)) <= m^k < n^(floor(k log(m)/log(n))+1), apply monotonicity and additivity, divide by k, and pass to the limit.
A1.atomicity: N^times is the free abelian monoid on the primes; rational relations among log(p) contradict unique factorisation.
A1.necessity_conclusion: Primes are automatic generators only after a canonical integer-labelled multiplicative composition law has been derived.
